guarantees.claim: When sel_mux is MuxFifo, keccak_valid_o is deasserted if hold_msg or en_msgbuf is high or msg_valid_i is low; else asserted.
When sel_mux is MuxPrefix, MuxFuncPad, or MuxZeroEnd, keccak_valid_o is driven to the same value as fsm_keccak_valid.
For all other values of sel_mux (including MuxNone), keccak_valid_o is forced to 0.

assumptions.claim: sel_mux is one-hot encoded and must match exactly one of the four explicit case items (MuxFifo, MuxPrefix, MuxFuncPad, MuxZeroEnd) or none (default). No multiple matches should occur.
assumptions.risk: If sel_mux has multiple bits set, the unique case may cause simulation/synthesis mismatch, potentially asserting keccak_valid_o when it should be 0 or vice versa.

assumptions.claim: In MuxFifo mode, msg_valid_i, hold_msg, and en_msgbuf must be stable glitch-free inputs to avoid spurious transitions on keccak_valid_o.
assumptions.risk: A combinational glitch on any of these signals could produce a false keccak_valid_o pulse, potentially violating downstream handshake contracts.
